response:
The concept of externalities refers to the unintended effects that occur when the actions of one individual directly impact others without those effects being accounted for in market transactions. Externalities can be either positive (benefits) or negative (costs). In sections 8.1 and 8.2, externalities are defined as impacts on others not reflected in market interactions between buyers and sellers.

In the context of the tragedy of the commons, externalities contribute to market failures because self-interested actors deplete shared resources without considering the broader environmental impact. This leads to collective action causing ecological depletion through collective action, necessitating coercive regulation to prevent tragedy.
